web_evidence.title: Doctor Zhivago - Penguin Random House Library Marketing
web_evidence.note: The publisher's authorized Part One excerpt sustains external third-person narration of Yura and other characters, including access to Yura's memories and feelings.

web_evidence.title: Pojmat' zhivoe: Antropomorfismer i Boris Pasternaks Doktor Zhivago
web_evidence.note: This University of Oslo scholarly study explicitly identifies the prose as third-person, distinguishes it from Zhivago's attributed poems, and explains that the form permits movement among the large cast.

web_evidence.title: The Metaphor in the Narrative Structure (Based on B. Pasternak's Novel Doctor Zhivago)
web_evidence.note: The peer-reviewed narratological study describes the novel's narrator as impersonal and its indirect narration as shifting among characters' viewpoints, supporting a nonparticipating controlling narrator.

web_evidence.title: Dr. Zhivago Study Guide
web_evidence.note: The opened study-guide overview explicitly states that the novel is narrated from a third-person omniscient point of view.

web_evidence.title: Доктор Живаго · War in Other Words
web_evidence.note: The University of Exeter collection provides a cited interior extract from page 107 that externally narrates Gordon and villagers in third person, corroborating the opening and Goodreads passages.

search_log: Searched "Doctor Zhivago Boris Pasternak excerpt publisher third person narrator" and opened the Penguin Random House authorized excerpt and the NPR/VPM excerpt.

Searched "Doctor Zhivago narrative point of view third person omniscient scholarly" and opened scholarly narratological sources from Tomsk State Pedagogical University, the University of Oslo/ResearchGate, and Slavic Review.

Searched exact phrases "Doctor Zhivago" "third-person narrator" and "Doctor Zhivago" "third person narration"; opened Course Hero's explicit whole-book description and the University of Pittsburgh dissertation result, whose preview was inaccessible.

Searched publisher, Google Books, Internet Archive, and library/repository routes; Google Books previews were non-English or limited, and no usable Internet Archive edition surfaced, while Penguin Random House and the University of Exeter supplied usable prose.

Checked for frame, diary, epistolary, multiple-narrator, and alternating-person complications; scholarly evidence instead distinguishes the third-person prose narrative from the concluding poems attributed to Zhivago.
person_note: The controlling prose narrator is nonparticipating and third-person, moving among Yury, Lara, and other characters and sometimes entering their consciousness. Multiple sustained Goodreads event passages independently show that pattern, while the authorized opening and scholarly whole-book analyses corroborate it. First- and second-person material in the quote set is dialogue, gnomic address, free-indirect/generalized 'you,' or local embedded expression. Scholarly evidence specifically distinguishes the prose portions, which are about Yury in third person, from the concluding poems attributed to Yury; those poems do not create an alternating base prose narration. No credible contrary structural evidence was found.
